content.content: 1→# Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO) 2→ 3→This repository contains the code and released models for our paper [SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14734). We propose a simpler and more effective preference optimization algorithm than DPO (Direct Preference Optimization) without using a reference model. SimPO outperforms DPO and its latest variants across AlpacaEval 2, MT-Bench, and Arena-Hard benchmarks under various settings. Please find all the released model checkpoints at [this link](https://huggingface.co/collections/princeton-nlp/simpo-66500741a5a066eb7d445889). 4→ 5→ 6→ 7→## 🆕 Changelog 8→- **[2024.10.12]** To facilitate reproducibility, we release the training curves for Llama3-Instruct and Gemma2-IT: 9→ - [Llama3-Instruct-SimPO](https://wandb.ai/yumeng0818/simpo/runs/zoesxyuj) 10→ - [Llama3-Instruct-SimPO v0.2](https://wandb.ai/yumeng0818/simpo/runs/zvv56fcj) 11→ - [Gemma2-IT-SimPO](https://wandb.ai/yumeng0818/simpo/runs/4w25j650) 12→- **[2024.07.17]** We released a new SimPO model [gemma-2-9b-it-SimPO](https://huggingface.co/princeton-nlp/gemma-2-9b-it-SimPO) by fine-tuning Google's gemma-2 9B model using on-policy [UltraFeedback data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/gemma2-ultrafeedback-armorm) annotated by [ArmoRM](https://huggingface.co/RLHFlow/ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1), achieving a **72.4** LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2 (**#[1 on the Leaderboard](https://tatsu-lab.github.io/alpaca_eval/)** 🎉🎉) and a **59.1** win rate on Arena-Hard! Please find the training script [here](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO/blob/main/training_configs/gemma-2-9b-it-simpo.yaml) and the data generation scripts [here](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO/tree/main/on_policy_data_gen)! 13→- **[2024.07.08]** We updated our paper ([v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14734v2)) 14→ - Additional baselines (RRHF, SLiC-HF, CPO) 15→ - New Llama3-Instruct setting (v0.2) with [ArmoRM](https://huggingface.co/RLHFlow/ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1) as the preference label annotator, yielding a better-performing model, [Llama-3-Instruct-8B-SimPO-v0.2](https://huggingface.co/princeton-nlp/Llama-3-Instruct-8B-SimPO-v0.2), with a **53.7** LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2 and a **36.5** win rate on Arena-Hard ([training script](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO/blob/main/training_configs/llama-3-8b-instruct-simpo-v2.yaml))! 16→ - [SimPO trainer](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO/blob/main/scripts/simpo_trainer.py) update for better reproducibility. The hyperparameter `gamma` changed to `gamma_beta_ratio` for easier tuning. 17→ 18→## 🔗 Quick Links 19→- [SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward](#simple-preference-optimization-simpo) 20→ - [Changelog](#-changelog) 21→ - [Tips for Running SimPO](#tips-for-running-simpo) 22→ - [Released Models](#released-models) 23→ - [Install Requirements](#install-requirements) 24→ - [Training scripts](#training-scripts) 25→ - [Evaluation](#evaluation) 26→ - [Bugs or Questions?](#bugs-or-questions) 27→ - [Citation](#citation) 28→ 29→## Tips for Running SimPO 30→Given the various inquiries about SimPO, we provide a list of tips to help you reproduce our paper results and achieve better outcomes for running SimPO on your own tasks. 31→ 32→### Environment 33→We provide an [environment file](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO/blob/main/environment.yml) including the python package versions we used in our experiments. For optimal reproducibility, we recommend using the same package versions. However, please note that results may still vary due to differences in hardware configurations and CUDA versions, etc. 34→ 35→### Hyperparameter tuning 36→Hyperparameter tuning is crucial for SimPO (and other preference optimization algorithms in general). The three main hyperparameters of SimPO to focus on are `learning_rate`, `beta`, and `gamma` (we recommend keeping the total batch size fixed at 128). 37→- `learning_rate`: It is the most critical hyperparameter for preference optimization. A large learning rate (e.g., 1e-5) can significantly degrade performance, causing the model to produce incoherent sentences or completely repetitive responses. We recommend grid searching over 3e-7, 5e-7, 8e-7, and 1e-6, if resources allow. **We find that a smaller learning rate (e.g., 5e-7) is more suitable for reasoning intensive domains like math for both DPO and SimPO.** 38→- `beta`: Beta controls the reward scaling between winning and losing responses. SimPO requires a much larger `beta` than DPO. In our preprint, we used a beta of `2.0` or `2.5`, but in many cases, an even larger beta (e.g., `10`) could yield better results. 39→- `gamma`: Gamma controls the target reward margin. We suggest tuning the ratio of gamma to beta (i.e., `gamma / beta`). We recommend using `0.5` as a starting point for `gamma_beta_ratio` and grid searching between `0` and `1`. A well-tuned `gamma_beta_ratio` can provide a modest improvement, but it is not as critical as other hyperparameters. 40→ 41→We used the following hyperparameters for training the released models (note that in our latest update, we changed the hyperparameter `gamma` to `gamma_beta_ratio` as the latter is normalized and easier to tune under different `beta` values). 42→| Setting | β | γ/β | Learning rate | 43→|-------------------|-----|-----|----------------| 44→| Mistral-Base | 2.0 | 0.8 | 3e-7 | 45→| Mistral-Instruct | 2.5 | 0.1 | 5e-7 | 46→| Llama3-Base | 2.0 | 0.5 | 6e-7 | 47→| Llama3-Instruct | 2.5 | 0.55 | 1e-6 | 48→| Llama3-Instruct v0.2 | 10 | 0.3 | 1e-6 | 49→| Gemma | 10 | 0.5 | 8e-7 | 50→ 51→For DPO, the best hyperparameters for each setting are as follows. 52→| Setting | β | Learning Rate | 53→|------------------------|------|---------------| 54→| Mistral-Base | 0.01 | 5e-7 | 55→| Mistral-Instruct | 0.01 | 5e-7 | 56→| Llama3-Base | 0.01 | 5e-7 | 57→| Llama3-Instruct | 0.01 | 7e-7 | 58→| Llama3-Instruct v0.2 | 0.01 | 3e-7 | 59→| Gemma | 0.01 | 5e-7 | 60→ 61→ 62→### Training and evaluation consistency in BOS 63→Our released Llama3 models use the initial version of the Llama3 tokenizer (prior to this [PR](https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct/commit/339ce92d052f002cdbac4a4bd551d1c61dd8345e)). We have found that the updated Llama3 tokenizer with vLLM occasionally introduces two BOS tokens, which can affect evaluation results. Therefore, please ensure that only one BOS token is included in the prompt after applying the Llama3 chat template during any evaluation. 64→ 65→*Notably, if you are training Llama3 and evaluating the trained models on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard using the templates provided in this repo, please make sure to use the pre-update Llama3 tokenizer (i.e., the one before the PR).* 66→ 67→### Reproducing AlpacaEval 2 numbers 68→Please make sure that you use `alpaca-eval==0.6.2` and [model configurations](https://github.com/princeton-nlp/SimPO/tree/main/eval/alpacaeval2/configs) in our repo for successfully reproducing AlpacaEval 2 results. AlpacaEval has a major revision for vllm decoding since `0.6.3` and causes a discrepancy from our experiments. 69→ 70→### Adding an extra SFT loss 71→The [CPO_SIMPO](https://github.com/fe1ixxu/CPO_SIMPO/tree/main) repository did preliminary experiments and observed that in some cases, adding an additional SFT loss can help improve results. In our own experiments, the SFT regularization helps preserve the reasoning ability (e.g., GSM8K) but degrades chat performance. If you'd like to apply SFT regularization, you can set `sft_weight` to be a positive value (by default it's 0). 72→ 73→ 74→## Released Models 75→ 76→### Gemma 77→We release the following two models that are built on top of the strong [google/gemma-2-9b-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-9b-it) model by training DPO and SimPO on the on-policy dataset [princeton-nlp/gemma2-ultrafeedback-armorm](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/gemma2-ultrafeedback-armorm). For GSM and MMLU, we use the [ZeroEval](https://github.com/yuchenlin/ZeroEval) repository which aims to evaluate instruction-tuned LLMs (i.e., chat models instead of base models) for their zero-shot performance on reasoning and knowledge heavy tasks. This demonstrates that the [google/gemma-2-9b-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-9b-it) model is more suitable for continued preference optimization. 86→- SimPO and DPO perform comparably across all benchmarks, but SimPO is inherently simpler and less resource-intensive. 87→ 88→ 89→### v0.2 90→We found that using a strong reward model for annotating preference optimization datasets is crucial. In this iteration, we have reannotated the dataset [princeton-nlp/llama3-ultrafeedback-armorm](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/llama3-ultrafeedback-armorm) using a more powerful reward model, [RLHFlow/ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1](https://huggingface.co/RLHFlow/ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1). To address this, we developed SimPO models based on the [google/gemma-2-9b-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-9b-it). Discrepancy between reward and generation for DPO.

ranking accuracy in terms of average log-likelihood, even after extensive preference optimization.

Limitations
More in-depth theoretical analysis. Despite the empirical success and intuitive motivation of
SimPO, a more rigorous theoretical analysis is necessary to fully understand the factors contributing

by pushing the margin between the average log likelihood of the winning response and the losing
response to exceed a target reward margin. However, it does not explicitly consider safety and honesty
aspects, which are crucial for real-world applications. Future work should explore integrating safety
and honesty constraints into SimPO to ensure that the generated responses are not only high-quality

## SimPO Loss Function - Complete Report

### Exact Mathematical Formula

The SimPO loss function is defined in **Equation (6)** from the paper:

```
L_SimPO(π_θ) = -E_{(x,y_w,y_l)~D} [ log σ( (β/|y_w|) log π_θ(y_w|x) - (β/|y_l|) log π_θ(y_l|x) - γ ) ]
```

Where:
- **σ** is the sigmoid function
- **β** is the reward scaling parameter (controls the reward magnitude)
- **γ** (gamma) is the target reward margin parameter (controls the minimum margin between winning and losing responses)
- **|y_w|** is the length of the winning (chosen) response
- **|y_l|** is the length of the losing (rejected) response
- **log π_θ(y|x)** is the log probability of the sequence under the policy model
- **E_{(x,y_w,y_l)~D}** is the expectation over preference pairs from dataset D

### Key Components

1. **Implicit Reward Function** (Equation 4):
   ```
   r_SimPO(x, y) = (β/|y|) log π_θ(y | x) = (β/|y|) Σ_{i=1}^{|y|} log π_θ(y_i | x, y_{<i})
   ```
   - Length-normalized average log probability
   - No reference model required (unlike DPO)
   - Directly aligns with generation metric

2. **Bradley-Terry Objective with Target Margin** (Equation 5):
   ```
   p(y_w ≻ y_l | x) = σ(r(x, y_w) - r(x, y_l) - γ)
   ```

### Implementation Parameters (from simpo_config.py)

- **beta** (`float`, defaults to 2.0): The reward scaling factor
- **gamma_beta_ratio** (`float`, defaults to 0.25): The ratio γ/β for easier hyperparameter tuning
- **label_smoothing** (`float`, defaults to 0): Label smoothing factor
- **loss_type** (`str`, defaults to "sigmoid"): Can be "sigmoid" or "hinge"
- **sft_weight** (`float`, defaults to 0.0): Optional SFT loss regularization weight

### Loss Type Variants

The code supports two loss variants through the `loss_type` parameter:

1. **Sigmoid Loss (default)**:
   ```
   L = -log σ(reward_diff - γ)
   ```

2. **Hinge Loss**:
   ```
   L = max(0, γ - reward_diff)
   ```

### Key Differences from DPO

SimPO improves upon DPO by:
1. Using average log probability as reward (length-normalized)
2. Eliminating the need for a reference model during training
3. Adding an explicit target reward margin (γ) to improve generalization
